service.description: The readiness checks the caller may read: each registered provider whose required permission the caller holds, called as the caller, its answer read as checks with a state (ready, warning, failed, unavailable), a reason code, a message, whom or what it is for (subject) and the scope that narrows to it, the checked time, the freshness facet of a data source (watermark, expected frequency, lag; stale past its lag), for a check that is not ready the owner's fix place as a key with its record and parameters (fixRoute, fixId, fixParameters: the application showing it resolves the key; never a URL), and the refresh registered for the provider when the caller may run it. A provider that fails is named in failedProviders and shown unavailable, without its diagnostics, while the others answer; one the caller may not read, or whose service refuses the caller, is left out. Narrowed by provider, owner app, group, state and scope: scopeParameters reach a provider only by the names its registration lists, and a provider that takes none of those asked is left out; instanceOnly leaves out every provider whose registration names a scope parameter (the checks of an organization or a store), which is what the System home's attention list asks. Needs a signed-in user; exposed to the Assistant and MCP by an app that registers it.

parameter.name: ownerOptions
parameter.description: The owner apps of the providers the caller may read

service.description: Run a registered refresh operation by its key: refused without the registration's own permission (REFRESH_DENIED) and for a key not registered or naming a missing service (REFRESH_UNAVAILABLE). Calls the owner's service as the caller with the registration's key, the operation key, the reason and only the scope parameters the registration names, which the owner checks; never a service or index name from the request. Answers a safe result: requested, or failed when the owner's service fails or refuses.

What needs attention and the health cards: attention, the checks of get#Readiness that are not ready, worst first, at most ten; and cards, failed job runs and sign-in failures of the last day, system messages in error and backup coverage, each {key, title, value, icon, route, routeId, parameters} with the key of the place that lists it, a count that cannot be read shown unavailable. Refuses a caller without ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW (PERMISSION_DENIED).

The readiness and support summary, the one projection of the support summary screen, its print and its redacted JSON: the instance (display name, framework version and package, when prepared and, unless redacted, by whom), the readiness checks the caller may read (get#Readiness), the protocols' states (ConfigurationServices.get#ProtocolReadiness) and the effective settings (get#EffectiveSettings, a secret only set or not), each section read with the caller's own permissions and marked unavailable with its reason when refused. No environment, host facts, listeners, paths, users, fix places, scopes or diagnostics. Redacted also leaves out who prepared it, writes an email address as [address] and says of a setting that names the server's inside only whether it is set. Refuses a caller without ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW (PERMISSION_DENIED).

The settings index: the owners' registered settings landings the caller may open, each shown only when its screen (the registration's screenLocation) opens to the caller's own groups, as the framework decides a screen path, and its view permission holds; with its owner, group, scope, who configures it, the key of its place (destinationRoute, which the application showing the index resolves) and the readiness provider of what it configures. Searched by text (title, description, owner, who configures), by owner app and by group. Needs a signed-in user: one who opens no destination is answered none.

One of the framework's own readiness checks, the provider its registration names (admin.mailServer, admin.backup, admin.reportMail, admin.reportAlertTopic, admin.adminFactors, admin.jobRuns, admin.cluster, admin.telemetry, admin.protocols, constitution.global), answering the readiness contract's checks; it reads the framework's own records and names no host, address or person. On a fresh instance the backup check warns that the nightly job is paused and that its mirror has no sendUrl. Refuses a caller without ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW (admin.protocols asks what ConfigurationServices.get#ProtocolReadiness asks instead) and an unknown check.
